block.title: vertical shaft of falling prisms
block.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, vertical poster composition, subtle CRT scanline glow. A deep vertical shaft inside the crystal labyrinth, camera pulled back to show the full terrible height: from the top of the frame the OPTION HUNTER descends bow-first like a violet guillotine blade, grapple-claws folded tight for the dive, launch bay dark; below it a constellation of HALO CRYSTALS hangs in the shaft at staggered heights, each a big faceted violet gem with its turning ring of six lilac satellites, their combined glow lighting the walls in bands of purple and pale violet; from the bottom edge the KESTREL rises in diagonal flight, steel-blue dart shape with a bold blue stripe, cyan canopy and a bright orange engine flare, blue bullets climbing in a tight zipper toward the nearest halo, whose ring crystals are flickering apart as it charges a radial burst of pink needles. Between the two forces a slow cloud of GLINT MOTES drifts — thousands of tiny crystal sparks, each throwing its own miniature star-glitter — turning the whole shaft into a shimmering veil that both sides shoot through. The triangle-facet walls of the shaft repeat the light down its length like a broken periscope. Deep-navy at the shaft's far top and bottom, never pure black. No text, no UI elements.
block.negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, watermark, blurry, pure black background, soft pastel palette, organic coral, human figures, horizontal composition, single floating crystal
block.notes: Color reference: shaft banded #8a48e8 into #c8a0ff, mote glitter white-lilac, kestral stripe #3858f0. Vertical dive composition — thief above, prey below — gives the encounter a natural menace gradient; the mote veil in the middle third is what keeps the frame Prism-Labyrinth rather than generic purple cave.
